openings.claim: Move location resolution from the clerk's repeated searches to fixed numbered parking zones on the existing shelves and cart, with a behind-desk paper reader-to-zone index. A hold remains at its assigned address until handoff; surname is a lookup key, not its storage address. This evaluates a bounded probe, not a proven evening intervention.
openings.delta: Divider cards carry stable physical addresses instead of surname ranges. The index covers shelf and cart holds together, replacing temporary-location exceptions. Keeping books stationary prevents the index becoming stale through shelving moves. Maintenance requires recording each arrival and removing collected entries; the clerk still establishes the correct reader association, verifies entitlement, retrieves and hands over the book.
openings.prediction: If moving locations and surname placement cause delays, indexed stationary holds should require fewer second-location searches, including household-name cases, without requiring cart-to-shelf transfers. The whole-window target remains at least 95% within two minutes and no wrong-reader handoffs.
openings.rival_prediction: The nearest alternative is correcting surname placement and refreshing the exception slip. If surname errors alone explain delays, that alternative should reduce searches comparably; fixed addresses would add indexing work without a distinct benefit.
openings.defeat: Defeat the proposal if accurately indexed stationary holds still require repeated searches, address congestion causes comparable delays, any wrong-reader handoff occurs, or preparation and necessary locator corrections exceed ten clerk-minutes.
openings.probe: Trial numbered zones for a bounded evening cohort using existing divider cards, paper and timing sheet, keeping identifying entries behind the desk. Record preparation plus locator maintenance time, arrival volume, book sizes, second searches and pickup durations. Compare with corrected surname placement and refreshed exceptions on a comparable window. Assess the full evening target separately from cohort performance.
assumptions: Existing divider cards can define usable addresses without additional furniture.
Arrival volume and book sizes permit stable parking through the evening.
An authoritative reader association can be established without relying solely on the possibly incorrect household surname.
Complete daily preparation and required locator maintenance can fit within ten clerk-minutes; the stipulated eight-minute preparation does not establish this.
